findings.what: The prices log is not log-only under return_chance eviction: it changes which host leaf eviction takes. PriceMeter.on_host_evicted asks ReturnChanceStrategy.holding_rate for each victim just before it goes, and that method (next_use_eviction.py:329) resolves the session with _session_registration, which adopts nodes into sessions as it ranks them. The same holds for every switch that turns the measuring on (MEASURED_PRICES, LATENESS_WEIGHT, READ_LINE), in mode observe too; under MEASURED_PRICES next_victim_price and next_host_victim rank leaves every 0.5 s with the same side effect. environ.py:365 says 'Logging only: no decision reads it' and the report says the log changes no decision; its side-by-side replay runs on fake caches that never call the observer from the eviction loop.
findings.scenario: I ran the copy's own FullComponent.drive_host_eviction with a real ReturnChanceStrategy, once with no observer and once with the observer a prefetcher installs in mode observe with only SGLANG_LOG_HICACHE_PRICES_INTERVAL set. Tree: root -> P -> {A, B} and root -> U; A and B are the tails of ended sessions, P and U are unregistered, U was used before P; 12 host tokens asked, 4 a node. Switches off: A, B, U. Log on: A, B, P. With the observer B is ranked again when it is popped, after A went, so it is P's only child and P is adopted into B's session; without it B is ranked only when the heap is built, while P has two children. Second case (B likely back, the first pass frees A and B, then an un-hinted V joins): off evicts P next, log on evicts V. Campaign 34's ec_full and ec_exact run return_chance, so a log-only repeat of either is not a like-for-like run. Reproduce with /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/design_unified_1126/impl/A/review_style_tests/zz_review_style_logonly_eviction.py (output in logonly_run2.out beside it).
findings.fix: Give ReturnChanceStrategy a read-only way to resolve a node's registration (the lookups of _session_registration without adopt and without dropping the parent's entry) and use it in holding_rate; rank without adopting in next_host_victim too. Add both cases to test_next_use_eviction.py: the eviction order is the same with and without an observer that calls holding_rate.

findings.what: FREE_EMPTY_LOOKUPS: five behaviours have no test. Each one-line regression below, applied in memory, passes all five changed test files. The first is a guard against an exception on the scheduler thread.
findings.scenario: (1) Dropping `and matched_tokens < len(key)` in _history_tokens: the first gate call of a turn whose match is longer than its plan's key then raises IndexError in RadixKey.match_at. No test calls the prompt gate with such a match; with the guard it answers covered (checked with matched = KEY_TOKENS + 500). (2) `found = hit_tokens > 0` at 1852: a hit under the 256-token threshold, which the cache revokes, stays charged. (3) Dropping `plan.refetch_capped = False` at 1865: a refunded turn stays capped. (4) Dropping `plan.lookup_charged = False` at 1696, or marking a room retry as a charged refetch at 863: a free room retry's empty answer then gives back a lookup charged before it, or a refetch that was never counted. (5) Deleting the ntp_lookup log call at 1867: no test reads the new line.
findings.fix: Add to TestFreeEmptyLookups: a prompt-gate call with a match past the key; an answer with hit = 128; a turn capped after two re-evictions whose last lookup answers empty; one case with SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_ROOM_RETRY also on; an assertion on the fields of the ntp_lookup line.

findings.what: The measuring (the prices log, or any switch that turns it on): five behaviours have no test; each regression below passes all five test files. The first is a guard against an exception on the scheduler thread.
findings.scenario: (1) `if plan is None:` in place of `if plan is None or self._return_chance is None:`: under next_use eviction a landing for a planned turn whose session tail is registered then calls adopt on None (AttributeError). The guard works (checked on MeasuredCache with tail_node_id=5), but no test has the measuring on, a session tail and a landing together. (2) Dropping `plan is not None or handle.rid in self._queued` at 1435: landing times are kept for every request and never removed. (3) `if False:` at 770: queued turns with no plan get no predicted wait, so their admissions never reach the error bins the hold reads. (4) `if not reader or landed_after is None:` at next_turn_meter.py:236: a reader whose landing was not seen feeds the error of the GPU turn. (5) `return 1` for an aborted request at 895: aborts count as admissions in c.
findings.fix: Add to TestMeasuredPrices: a landing under NextUseStrategy with a registered tail; a landing for an unknown rid leaves _landed_at empty; an unplanned queued turn's admission lands in the error bins; a reader with no landing feeds neither side; an aborted turn leaves c where it was.

findings.what: MEASURED_PRICES: the room price measured at the eviction frontier never reaches a staging in any test, and the next victim's price is tested on its first pricing only and under next_use eviction only.
findings.scenario: These pass all five test files: `return self._meter.next_victim_price(self._load, now)` in _staging_price (the frontier's price dropped); pricing the victim once and never again (next_turn_meter.py:186); `return queued` for a registration queued longer than QUEUED_MAX_AGE_S (next_use_eviction.py:209 and 334); dropping the ceiling on the victim's price (next_turn_meter.py:200). In TestMeasuredRoomPrice no eviction is ever observed, so the frontier's price is 0 throughout; each subtest builds a new prefetcher and ticks once; and MeasuredCache evicts by next_use while the expected-cost arms run return_chance.
findings.fix: In TestMeasuredRoomPrice: observe an eviction and assert ec_start's price is the frontier's when that is above the victim's; change the victim and assert the price follows only after VICTIM_PRICE_INTERVAL_S; run one case with a ReturnChanceStrategy on the cache. In test_next_use_eviction.py add a stale queued registration with queued= given.

findings.what: test_the_harm_of_a_refused_read_is_its_recompute_at_the_fitted_cost_times_mu cannot tell the fitted prefill cost from the constant it replaces (amendment A5 in the harm charge).
findings.scenario: No prefill is observed in the test, so the fit is at its seed, which is RECOMPUTE_S_PER_TOKEN: replacing `self._meter.prefill_cost.seconds(...)` by `lost_tokens * RECOMPUTE_S_PER_TOKEN` at next_turn_prefetch.py:1597 passes all five test files. The other half is pinned: pricing the harm at the queue count instead of mu fails this test. The fit's forgetting is also untested: `fade = 1.0` in PrefillCostModel.observe passes.
findings.fix: Install a PrefillCostModel with other coefficients before the refusal (as RecomputeTestCase does) and assert harm_ms from it. Add a pure case in which 400 fast prefills follow 400 slow ones and the fit moves.

findings.what: The prices line (amendments A1 and A4): only rid, plans, queued, waiting, ready, late and parked are asserted by name. The report says the test is red when a field is missing or moved; it is not.
findings.scenario: These pass all five test files: deleting `mu=` (269) or `kappa=` (274); deleting `**self._read_path_fields()` (292), which removes lookup_ms, lag_ms, whold_ms and the four hold counters A4 asks for; reporting the hold counters as running totals instead of per-line deltas (317). No test builds a prefetcher with the log on and no read scheduler. I ran that branch (a fifo fake and the real CPU cache, modes observe and on): it logs 'na' for the read-path fields without error.

findings.what: RECOMPUTE_WHEN_STARVED (amendment A3): five parts of the rule have no test.
findings.scenario: These pass all five test files: counting ready turns with the 0.5 s debounce (`self._prices.ready_waiting > 0` in place of `self._meter.ready_since`), which A3 rules out in words; not resetting _starved_since when a ready turn appears; acting before the lags are measured (dropping `or not self._line_measured` at 1776); dropping the write hold from a timed read's landing (1790-1791); dropping `if plan.recompute: return False` in _check_queued (1005), after which the queue check asks for the prefetch of a turn that gave its read up every 0.5 s.
findings.fix: Add to TestRecomputeWhenStarved: a turn that became ready 0.2 s ago keeps every read; starved, ready, starved again needs another 0.5 s; unmeasured lags keep the read; a write hold turns a kept read into a dropped one; after the drop tick() returns no refetch for the turn while its history is missing.

findings.what: READ_LINE: the write-hold allowance (the plan's part 3) is tested as a pure method only, not where the prefetcher adds it; the pages ntp_due logs are not asserted; under expected-cost staging only a read needed now is ever in the line.
findings.scenario: These pass all five test files: deleting `seconds += cache.read_lags.write_hold_left_s(now)` in _line_seconds, adding it for reads needed now as well (`if True:`), or doubling it; computing the queue check's load without the line (1028-1034); logging the launched pages in ntp_due for a just-in-time start (1266), although the plan says backlog_pages becomes the line's pages; `deadline=None` in _staged_start (1404), so a staging counts only the reads needed now.
findings.fix: In TestReadLine: with a write hold on (note_write_hold), a timed start moves earlier by what is left of it and a read needed now does not; assert backlog_pages of ntp_due for a queued and a pending turn. In TestReadLineByExpectedCost park a timed read due earlier instead of one needed now.

findings.what: Amendments A1 and A2: the arrivals term of mu_for and the line in the gate's read time are tested on hand-built inputs only, not as the prefetcher feeds them.
findings.scenario: These pass all five test files: `arrival_rate=0.0` in _follow_prices, so mu_for never counts the turns that arrive during a recompute (the point of the study's finding 3c); a read time for the recompute quote without the pages ahead (`self._line_load.seconds(own_pages=..., backlog_pages=0)` at 1755). In RecomputeTestCase nothing was admitted in the last minute and nothing is launched or parked when the gate is asked.
findings.fix: In TestRecomputeByPrice: admit 30 turns in the last minute, then assert mu in ntp_gate is above 1 and a 24K-token history reads; park a 2,000-page read needed now and assert a history that read before is recomputed.

verdict:
**Switches off: safe by this lens.** The three frozen classes are byte-identical to the base copy and no switch is read at import. The five changed test files and the four untouched ones pass with the reported counts (re-run), and every pre-existing test is unmodified. Nothing I probed changes with the switches off.

**Switches on: not yet.**
- **The prices log changes decisions.** Under return_chance eviction, the policy of ec_full and ec_exact, it changes which host leaf is evicted, and so does every switch that turns the measuring on. Until `holding_rate` stops adopting nodes, a log-only run is not a like-for-like repeat of its arm.
- **Much switched behaviour is unpinned.** 36 one-line regressions I applied in memory pass all five test files; 14 others were caught, three of them the engineer's own, used as controls. Two of the 36 remove guards against an exception on the scheduler thread.
- **Nothing has run on a real tree or a GPU.**

**What speaks for it.** 388 random 500-event scenarios with the switches on in valid combinations raised nothing on the fake cache; the starved rule fired 11 times and the gate answered recompute 12 times. The one exception the fuzz produced needs a landing before the first tick, which the Scheduler's loop cannot produce. The untested branches I ran also hold: fifo read order with the log, the log and the prompt gate on the real CPU cache, and a landing under next_use.

**Two notes.**
- Campaign 34's ec arms pass `--hicache-storage-next-turn-price-learning harm`, which MEASURED_PRICES refuses at startup by design, so those queue lines need `off`.
- Early on I ran one command outside the test recipe inside the container: `which` for lint tools and a Python import check. It used no GPU and touched nothing under /mnt/ssd.

My throwaway tests and their outputs are in /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/design_unified_1126/impl/A/review_style_tests/. The copies I placed in the copy's test folder are deleted, and nothing else in the copy or the real tree was touched.
